decisions.reason: As a versatile cardboard quarter-pallet display squarely within the firm's core capabilities, it remains a relatively low-cost offer to retain even though several years of market experience have reduced the remaining uncertainty.

Because this pegboard-back variant is more niche and has not remained visibly promoted, management would likely judge that enough has been learned about its limited payoff to reallocate resources to stronger core and new options.
The eighth-pallet format still extends the standard cardboard display range at modest incremental cost, so the firm would likely keep it as a useful core-adjacent option.

Being farther from the paper-based core and likely more burdensome to support, the wooden display pallet now looks like an option whose uncertainty has largely resolved without enough strategic value to justify keeping it.
